scenario: Humanitarian researchers examine only refugee settlement cooperatives that passed a minimum viability assessment. Mean cooperative member count is 62 (σ=13); the viability threshold is 40 members. The true mean membership across all cooperatives established in the assessment cohort is needed.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

values.note: Only units above the survival threshold appear in the observed sample

question: (a) Assuming cooperative member count is normally distributed with σ=13 members in the full pre-filter cohort, solve numerically for the true pre-filter population mean μ such that E[X | X > 40] = 62. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much (in members) does the survivor mean overstate μ? (d) What policy or scientific conclusion error arises from ignoring the survival filter?

ground_truth.explanation: The refugee settlement cooperatives in humanitarian research dataset is a truncated-normal sample above the survival threshold t=40 members. Solving E[X|X>t]=μ+σφ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=62 numerically gives μ=60.3902 members. Only 94.16% of the original cohort survived; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 1.6098 members. Ignoring the filter leads to over-estimating the baseline quality/capacity of the full cohort, producing over-optimistic policy conclusions.

naive_answer: The true mean cooperative member count is 62 members because that is the average observed among the surviving/studied units.
naive_trap: The observed sample consists only of units above the survival threshold. The observed mean is E[X|X>40] — a truncated conditional expectation — not the population mean. It systematically overstates μ whenever the threshold is non-trivially binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter ≡ truncated-normal sampling with lower truncation at t=40. (2) E[X|X>t] = μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ) / Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 62. (3) Solve numerically via brentq on [-285.0, 61.9999] → μ=60.3902. (4) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((40−60.3902)/13) = 0.94162. (5) Overstatement: 62−60.3902 = 1.6098 members.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 62,13,40
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-60.3902)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.94162)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-1.6098)<0.01
